# ghost_branches (Data Source)

Lists the branches of a Ghost repository, with the default branch and which branches an active `ghost_repository_ruleset` protects. Branch SHAs cost one API request per branch, so they are only fetched with `include_sha = true`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every branch of a repository.
data "ghost_branches" "all" {
  repository = "my-org/my-repo"
}

# Only the branches an active ruleset protects, with the commit each points
# at. include_sha costs one API request per branch.
data "ghost_branches" "protected" {
  repository              = "my-org/my-repo"
  only_protected_branches = true
  include_sha             = true
}

output "default_branch" {
  value = data.ghost_branches.all.default_branch
}

output "release_branches" {
  value = [for name in data.ghost_branches.all.names : name if startswith(name, "release/")]
}

output "protected_shas" {
  value = { for b in data.ghost_branches.protected.branches : b.name => b.sha }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repository` (String) The repository's full name, `owner/slug`, e.g. `ghost_repository.example.full_name`.

### Optional

- `include_sha` (Boolean) Whether to look up the commit each listed branch points at, which takes one API request per branch. Defaults to `false`, which leaves every `sha` null.
- `only_non_protected_branches` (Boolean) Keeps only the branches no active ruleset protects. Cannot be `true` together with `only_protected_branches`.
- `only_protected_branches` (Boolean) Keeps only the branches an active ruleset protects. Cannot be `true` together with `only_non_protected_branches`.

### Read-Only

- `branches` (Attributes List) The repository's branches, after the filters, ordered by name as Ghost orders them (byte order, so upper case comes first). Empty for a repository with no commits. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--branches))
- `default_branch` (String) The branch the repository opens on (git `HEAD`), null when nothing has been pushed yet. This is what the web UI shows, and it can differ from `ghost_repository`'s `default_branch`, which is the stored setting: for example when the first push was to a branch other than `main`, or the default branch was deleted over git.
- `id` (String) The repository's current full name, `owner/slug`. It differs from `repository` when that names a repository that has since been renamed.
- `names` (List of String) The `name` of each branch, in the same order as `branches`.
- `repository_id` (Number) The numeric ID of `repository`.

<a id="nestedatt--branches"></a>
### Nested Schema for `branches`

Read-Only:

- `default` (Boolean) Whether this is `default_branch`.
- `name` (String) The branch name, without the `refs/heads/` prefix, e.g. `feat/login`.
- `protected` (Boolean) Whether an active ruleset targets the branch. Rulesets in `evaluate` or `disabled` mode, and branches a ruleset excludes, don't count.
- `rules` (List of String) The rule types the active rulesets apply to the branch, combined and sorted, e.g. `["deletion", "pull_request"]`. Empty when it isn't protected.
- `sha` (String) The SHA of the commit the branch points at. Null unless `include_sha` is `true`.
